newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares jump 2.74pct as interest rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares jump 2.74pct as interest rates fall.

text.p: Greek shares climbed 2.74 percent on Thursday helped by a sharp rise in banks and a wide range of industrials which brokers justified on grounds of improved profitability and easing interest rates.

"Large caps such as National Bank and OTE set the trend for the broader market. Industrials which gathered momentum in recent sessions helped lift the index along with banks," said Mathios Doulos, a broker at Kyranis Securities.
The drop in interest rates favours profit growth on leveraged industrial companies and Treasury paper-rich banks, he added.
The Athens general index climbed 2.74 percent or 44.84 points to 1,683.85 from Wednesday's close at 1,639.01.
At the close 7.5 million shares had been traded, valued at 33 billion drachmas, including several blocks -- mostly in banks.
Advancers led decliners 174 to 53 with 29 stocks unchanged on 256 traded.
Greece will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.6 percent, down 10 basis points, on June 2.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,101-1,131. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, gained 195 drachmas to 6,700.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted higher at 704.88-749.87. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $94.43-$96.13. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,721-3,948 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $23.95-25.65. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 300-333 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
